mode.live.hint: Transmitting is possible. Use with care.
mode.listen.hint: Never transmits. Decode only, the radio can be in any mode.
mode.practice.hint: Never transmits. Practice against simulated stations, or just send with a sidetone.

mode.confirm.body: In LIVE mode CWLD can make your radio transmit. Check your antenna, power and frequency first.
banner.listen: Listening only. Nothing you type is sent to the radio.
banner.practice: Practice mode. Nothing leaves the application, sending is simulated.
banner.live: LIVE. Sending reaches the radio. Esc stops at once.

qso.name: Name

conversation.title: Conversation

settings.calls.help: Separate with commas. The first one is your main callsign.
settings.name: Your name
error.not_live: Sending is only possible in LIVE mode.
error.blocked: The transmit guard refused this command.

radio.title: Radio
radio.port.help: Windows: right-click the Start button, choose Device Manager, open Ports (COM and LPT) and look for your radio. Then pick that COM number here. The IC-7300 MK II shows two ports. Try the first one, and if the radio does not answer, try the other.
radio.address.help: On the radio: MENU, SET, Connectors, CI-V, CI-V Address. The default of the IC-7300 MK II is B6. Also check that CI-V Transceive is ON there, then CWLD sees every change of frequency at once.
radio.pipeline.help: Advanced. Off is safe: CWLD waits until a block of 30 characters is finished. On avoids a small gap, but only works if your radio accepts a second text while it is still sending. It switches itself off when the radio refuses.
radio.baud.help: For a USB cable this hardly matters. It must match the menu of the Icom if you changed it there.
radio.qmx.help: On the QMX, set Audio, Sidetone volume to a high value and Sidetone abs/rel to Relative, so CWLD can hear your own sidetone.
queue.title: Waiting to be sent
warning.civ_pipeline_off: The radio refused a second block, so sending early is switched off.
warning.civ_rejected: The radio keeps refusing the text. Is the mode CW and is Break-in on?
warning.no_answer: The radio does not answer. Check the cable, the port and the CI-V address.
warning.radio_not_transmitting: The radio does not transmit. Is Break-in on and the mode CW?
warning.qmx_rejected: The QMX did not understand a command.
warning.not_a_qmx: This does not look like a QMX. Is the right port chosen?
warning.dropped_chars: Some characters cannot be sent in CW and were left out.
error.word_too_long: One word is too long to send.
error.message_too_long: This text takes more than a minute to send. Shorten it.
swr.alert.title: SWR ALERT
swr.alert.body: SWR {swr} is above the limit of {limit}. Sending was stopped at once. Check the antenna and the coax before you transmit again.
swr.alert.qrx: QRX was sent after the stop.
swr.alert.ack: I checked the antenna, allow sending again
swr.title: SWR protection
swr.enabled: Stop at once when the SWR is too high
swr.enabled.help: CWLD reads the SWR from the radio while it transmits. After two readings in a row above the limit (about a fifth of a second) it stops the text and shows a red alert. Sending stays blocked until you confirm. This is a second line of protection, your radio has its own. Not every radio gives an SWR reading: the QMX does not yet.
swr.qrx: Also send QRX after the stop
swr.qrx.help: On by default: after the stop CWLD sends QRX as the very last transmission, so the other station knows you are leaving. It does transmit once more into the antenna with the high SWR, so switch it off if you would rather not.
swr.qmx_unverified: The QMX gives its SWR with the CAT command SW. This is not yet verified on a real radio, so test it at low power.
swr.paddle: A paddle transmission cannot be stopped by CWLD. Release the paddle.
error.swr_latched: Sending is blocked after an SWR alert. Check the antenna and confirm the alert first.
composer.placeholder.swr: Sending is blocked after the SWR alert
meter.confidence.help: How sure the decoder is about the last characters. This is an estimate, not a measured error rate.
meter.accuracy.help: Share of correct characters in practice mode. Here the keyed text is known, so this is the real accuracy.
audio.title: Audio and decoder
audio.input.help: The Icom IC-7300 MK II appears as "USB Audio CODEC". Turn off all sound enhancements for this input in Windows.
audio.tone.help: The tone the decoder listens to. Clicking a signal in the waterfall changes it.
audio.recdir.help: Leave empty for Documents\CWLD. Recordings are WAV files that CwGet can also decode.
audio.level.low: Very low level. Raise "USB AF Output Level" on the radio or the input level in Windows.
audio.level.high: Too loud, close to clipping. Lower the level on the radio or in Windows.
audio.overruns: {n} samples were lost because the computer was too busy.
audio.file.help: Full path of a 16 bit WAV file. It plays at real speed into the decoder, as if it came from the radio.
rec.start.help: Record the radio audio to a WAV file, for testing the decoder.
rec.stop.help: Stop the recording and save the file.
waterfall.click: Click a signal to decode it
waterfall.off: Audio is off. Start listening in Settings.
conversation.unsure: The decoder is not sure about these characters.
tabs.title: Conversations
tabs.new.help: Start a new conversation and clear the screen. The previous one stays in its tab.
tabs.live.help: The running conversation. New text arrives here.
tabs.old.help: An earlier conversation. You can read it and edit its details.
composer.placeholder.old: You are looking at an earlier conversation. Click the tab with the green dot to send.
audio.squelch.help: How clearly a signal must stand out of the noise before the decoder believes it. Higher is stricter: less text out of noise, but weak signals drop out. Default 3.5. If you see text without a signal, raise it. It works at once.
signal.help: Green: the decoder sees a clear signal at the set pitch. Grey: only noise, nothing is decoded.
audio.autotone: Find the strongest signal by itself
audio.autotone.help: When the pitch has been quiet for a while, the decoder jumps to the strongest CW signal in the waterfall (like GoMax in MRP40). After a click on the waterfall it stays put for 10 seconds. Weak signals (around 0 dB) it does not find by itself: click those.
update.title: Updates
update.error: Checking failed. Check your internet connection and try again later.
update.privacy: The check only fetches a file from GitHub. No personal data or callsigns are sent. The app restarts after updating.
tabs.wait.help: When the frequency changes by more than 500 Hz and stays there this long, a new tab starts. No tab is added while you turn the knob. Default 5, choose 1 to 30.
scope.title: Band scope
scope.click: Click a signal: the radio tunes there.
scope.waiting: Waiting for the radio's band scope. Connect the radio. On an Icom CWLD switches the scope data on by itself.
scope.out_of_range: The radio says: out of the scope's range.
view.title: View
view.band_scope.help: The spectrum as on the radio's screen (Icom only). Click a signal to go there.
view.audio_waterfall.help: Block on the right with what the decoder hears, inside the radio's filter. Click there to set the decoder on a tone.
audio.panel.title: Audio
audio.panel.help: What the decoder hears, inside the radio's filter. Click a signal to set the decoder on that tone.
qlib.title: Codes and abbreviations
qlib.hint: Click a code to add it to your message. Add a ? to make it a question.
qlib.noinsert: cannot be sent by the radio keyer
radio.autoconnect.help: CWLD connects to this radio by itself at start. Off: you press Connect yourself. If the radio is off at that moment, CWLD simply starts not connected.
settings.default_rst.help: The report CWLD puts in your messages: 5NN (cut number, as used in contests and pile-ups) or 599 (in full). You can still change it per QSO in the QSO panel.
settings.send.speed: The sending speed is set with the slider under the send box.
decoder.preset.title: How strict is the decoder?
decoder.preset.help: Weak also tries faint signals but may show some text out of noise. Strong reads only clear signals. These are three ready-made positions of the slider below, chosen by feel and not yet measured.
decoder.filter.help: Narrow follows the speed and is best for steady signals. Wide has double the bandwidth, for drifting or chirpy signals. The red lines in the audio waterfall show the filter.
decoder.afc.help: The decoder keeps itself exactly on the tone of the station, within 60 Hz. Key: F7.
decoder.gain.help: Raises or lowers the incoming audio for the decoder and the meter, from -20 to +20 dB. A recording stays as it came in. Better: set the level of the radio so the meter stays between 5 and 90 percent.
decoder.speed.title: Speed
decoder.speed.help: The decoder looks for speeds between slowest and fastest (5 to 60 WPM). A fixed speed (0 means automatic) is for beacons or a station that keys at a steady speed.
tabs.autoclose.help: A conversation without new text for this long closes by itself. 0 switches it off. The one you are in, and any with sent text that is not logged, never close by themselves.
tabs.closeall.help: Closes all conversations and keeps one new empty one
tabs.closeall.ask: {n} conversation(s) have sent text and are not logged yet. Close them all anyway?
contest.help: In contest mode the serial number {NR} is filled in for your messages. Outside contest mode {NR} stays empty.
contest.nr.help: Change it by hand if you need to, for example after a repeated QSO.
contest.later: Counting up after each logged QSO, the logbook and dupe warnings come with the logbook in a later version.
contest.ask: Contest mode was on before with number {nr} next. Continue there or start again at 1?
contest.chip.help: Switch contest mode on or off (serial number {NR})
pileup.title: Pile-up
meter.peak.help: The highest level of the incoming audio. Between 5 and 90 percent is good.
meter.peak.low: Too low: raise the audio level of the radio or the gain.
meter.peak.high: Too high: the sound card input is overloaded. Lower the audio level of the radio or the gain.
audio.panel.strongest.help: Once: move to the strongest keyed signal heard in the last seconds
status.searching.help: The radio does not answer (off, or the cable is out). CWLD tries again every few seconds.
status.simulator.help: CWLD is running on the built-in simulator. Nothing real is connected. Choose your radio in Settings, section Radio and SWR.
banner.noradio: No radio chosen yet: CWLD is running on a simulator, not on your radio.
contest.note.uba: UBA contest. Belgian stations send a report, a serial number from 001 and the UBA section (XXX if not a member). Stations outside Belgium send a report and a serial number.
contest.note.uba_old: UBA Spring Contest. The rules used here come from the 2023 page: check the current rules before the contest.
contest.note.winter: UBA Low Band Winter Contest. The rules used here come from a 2014 page: check the current rules. Belgian stations send a report and the section, without a serial number.
contest.note.cqww: CQ WW DX Contest. The rules count the use of a CW decoder as assistance: if you use CWLD, enter in a class with assistance.
contest.note.arrl: ARRL International DX Contest. DX stations may only work stations in the USA and Canada (W and VE). You send the report and your power.
contest.note.iaru: IARU HF Championship. CW and SSB are one contest. You send the report and your ITU zone (headquarters stations send their society).
contest.note.wae: WAE DX Contest. If a station sends no serial number, log it as 000. QTC messages are not supported yet.
contest.import.notjson: This file is not a readable export file.
contest.import.notexport: This file is not an export of CWLD contest profiles.
contest.profiles.title: Contest profiles
contest.builtin.hint: A built-in profile cannot be changed. Press Copy to make your own version, then change that.
contest.copy.name: {name} (copy)
contest.new.name: My contest
contest.invalid: A profile needs a name and at least one exchange.
contest.unsaved: You have unsaved changes. Save them first, or press the profile again to drop them.
contest.name: Name
contest.calls.help: Separate with commas, for example TEST UBA, CQ TEST. Each becomes a button that sends the call followed by your callsign.
contest.note.label: Note (shown when you choose the profile)
contest.sent.title: What you send
contest.sent.help: Use the variables {CALL}, {RST}, {NR} and your own ones, for example {SEC}. If you have more than one exchange (for example from Belgium and from abroad), you choose with a list on the main screen.
contest.sent.label: Name of this exchange
contest.cut: Cut numbers for the serial number
contest.cut.help: 0 is sent as T and 9 as N, so 019 becomes T1N. Use it only if the contest allows it. Off by default.
contest.recv.title: What you receive
contest.recv.help: One extra field that the other station sends, for example the section. It is used in the logbook, which comes in a later version. Here you only set it up.
contest.recv.on: This contest has an extra field
contest.recv.name: Short name
contest.recv.label: Description
contest.recv.prefixes.help: Leave empty if every station sends it. For example ON, OO, OP for Belgian stations.
contest.vars.title: Own variables
contest.vars.help: Fixed values you can use as {NAME} in every button and in the sending box, for example SEC with your section. The serial number {NR} counts by itself.
contest.vars.name: Name
contest.vars.bad: {name} is not a good name: use capitals, digits and an underscore, starting with a letter (at most 16).
contest.vars.reserved: {name} is used by CWLD itself. Choose another name.
contest.vars.dup: Two variables have the same name.
contest.backup.title: Backup and sharing
contest.backup.help: Save your own profiles and variables in a file. You can restore it later or share it with your club. The built-in profiles are not saved, they are always there.
contest.export.all: Export all my profiles and variables
contest.import.replace: Overwrite own profiles with the same name (otherwise a copy is added)
contest.run.help: Run: you call CQ and stations answer you.
contest.sp.help: S&P (search and pounce): you tune around and answer other stations.
contest.test.help: Test mode: QSOs go to a separate test log with its own number. Your real number and log stay untouched.
contest.test.clear.help: Removes every QSO of the test log for good. The real log is not touched.
contest.rate.help: QSOs per hour over the last 10 minutes, and the number of QSOs in the last 60 minutes.
contest.log.help: Writes this QSO to the log and raises your number.
contest.sug.help: Take over what the decoder heard in the reply. Press Tab in an empty field.
contest.unlogged: Number {nr} was sent to {call} but not logged.

export.utc: Times are UTC. Leave empty for no limit.
export.contestid.help: Written on contest QSOs. Check it against the official ADIF list before you rely on it.
conversation.word.help: Click to put this word in the entry line or the QSO panel

profile.name: Name

act.none.portable: You are portable: start an activation so the reference and grid go into every QSO.
act.midnight: This activation crosses midnight UTC. Many programs count each UTC day separately.
act.intro: A reference is optional. The grid is written into every QSO of this activation.
act.wwff.help: Format: two letters, FF, a dash and four digits.
act.grid.help.portable: Check this carefully: it is the grid of where you are now.

practice.title: Practice
practice.learn.help: Opens the morse learning app (letters, Koch method) in your browser.
practice.help.help: Off: the decoded text is hidden and nothing is filled in for you. You copy by ear.
practice.af: The stations come from the computer (headphones or speakers), not from the radio. Turn the AF knob of the radio down. Nothing is ever transmitted. QSOs go to the test log.
practice.score.title: Practice result
practice.score.summary: Wrong calls: {busted}. Wrong exchange: {wrong}. Completed but not logged: {missed}.
practice.problem.name: name
wiz.title: Welcome to CWLD
wiz.skip: Skip, I will do it later
wiz.again.help: Walk through the four setup steps again: radio, radio settings, sound and station.
wiz.s1.intro: Plug the radio into the computer with a USB cable and switch it on. Then choose which radio you have.
wiz.s1.found: CWLD chose this port for you. You can change it.
wiz.s1.none.title: No port found yet. Check these three things:
wiz.s1.none.1: The USB cable is a data cable, plugged into the radio and the computer.
wiz.s1.none.3: The Icom USB driver is installed. Open Device Manager (click the right mouse button on the Start button and choose Device Manager) and look for the radio under Ports (COM and LPT).
wiz.s1.several: More than one port may belong to the radio. The IC-7300 MK II shows two. Try the first one (Serial Port A, CI-V). If the radio does not answer, try the other.
wiz.s1.ok: Connected to {name}. The frequency is {freq} kHz.
wiz.s1.fail: The radio did not answer. Check the port and, for an Icom, the CI-V address (default B6).
wiz.s1.sim: With the simulator CWLD pretends to have a radio. You can listen to a recording or practise, and connect a real radio later in Settings.
wiz.s2.intro: Two settings in the radio make CWLD follow it live.
wiz.s2.civ: Switch CI-V Transceive on. On the radio press MENU, open SET, then Connectors, then CI-V, and set CI-V Transceive to ON. Menu names can differ a little between firmware versions.
wiz.s2.cant: CWLD cannot read this setting from the radio, so you check it yourself with the test below.
wiz.s2.test: Turn the main tuning knob of the radio a little.
wiz.s2.moved: The frequency followed the knob. Good.
wiz.s2.notmoved: Waiting for you to turn the knob.
wiz.s2.notmoved.help: If nothing changes after a few seconds, check that the radio is still connected and that CI-V Transceive is ON.
wiz.s2.qmx: The QMX needs no CI-V setting. It needs a loud sidetone, because CWLD listens to it. That is in the next step.
wiz.s2.sim: The simulator has nothing to check. Go on.
wiz.s3.intro: CWLD decodes the sound of the radio. Choose the input of the radio and watch the level bar.
wiz.s3.win.title: If the bar stays empty or the sound is poor, check Windows:
wiz.s3.win.1: Click Start, type microphone privacy and press Enter. Switch on Microphone access, Let apps access your microphone and Let desktop apps access your microphone.
wiz.s3.win.2: Open the sound settings of Windows, choose the USB Audio CODEC input and turn all audio enhancements off.
wiz.s3.win.3: Keep the Windows input level in the middle, then adjust the AF output on the radio until the bar is mostly in the green zone.
wiz.s3.qmx.title: QMX: set the sidetone
wiz.s3.qmx.body: In the menu of the QMX open Audio. Set Sidetone volume high, for example 99, and Sidetone abs/rel to Relative. Without a loud sidetone CWLD hears too little.
wiz.s4.intro: These details go into every QSO and into your messages. Callsigns are yours, CWLD has none built in.
wiz.s4.calls: Your callsigns, separated by commas. The first is the main one.
wiz.s4.test.title: Silent test
wiz.s4.test.body: This is what CWLD would send for a CQ at 18 words per minute. Nothing is transmitted now.
wiz.s4.mode: You start in LISTEN mode, which never transmits. You switch to LIVE yourself, and Esc always stops sending.
wiz.err.nocall: Fill in at least one callsign.
